name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development due to 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 17β-HSD3 Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual
Biochemical evidence of low testosterone to androstenedione ratio in serum or stimulated tests
Identification of pathogenic variants in the HSD17B3 gene by molecular genetic testing
Absence of Müllerian duct derivatives on imaging or surgery
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY individual plus biochemical confirmation of low testosterone to androstenedione ratio and identification of pathogenic HSD17B3 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by hormonal stimulation tests and imaging studies to exclude other causes of DSD.

laboratory: Low serum testosterone levels relative to androstenedione
Normal or elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence of testes in inguinal or abdominal position
Absence of Müllerian structures (uterus, fallopian tubes)
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue showing testicular tissue without Leydig cell hyperplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated testosterone with resistance to androgen action
Presence of female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype
Normal testosterone but low dihydrotestosterone (DHT) levels

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth in a 46,XY individual
Delayed or absent virilization during puberty
Family history of similar genital anomalies or consanguinity
references: Maimoun L, Philibert P, Cammas B, et al. 17β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 deficiency: clinical, biological, and molecular features. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2011;96(7):E1240-E1249.
Orphanet: 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 3 deficiency. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2020.
